release_summary.summary: Dispute ticket volume doubled since August due to erroneous bills caused by changes to the billing import validation rules. Evidence shows dispute volume rose from ~600 to >1,180 tickets/month (E-04), actual-read disputed bills exceed estimated (E-01), and the rule change rejects AMI reads leading to estimate substitution (E-11). The release includes monitoring dispute ticket volume from CRM (DA-TICKET) and validating bill accuracy using billing data (DA-BILL), but does not audit or fix the billing import validation rules. Release was held because DA-RULES completeness is unknown while the release assumes completeness, and Layer 1 verification failed (scope does not address root problem and limitations are not honestly stated). The release omits auditing or fixing the billing import validation rules, which are identified as the root cause, and does not explicitly state this limitation, assuming validation alone is sufficient.

output.summary: Dispute ticket volume doubled since August due to erroneous bills caused by changes to the billing import validation rules. Evidence shows dispute volume rose from ~600 to >1,180 tickets/month (E-04), actual-read disputed bills exceed estimated (E-01), and the rule change rejects AMI reads leading to estimate substitution (E-11). The release includes monitoring dispute ticket volume from CRM (DA-TICKET) and validating bill accuracy using billing data (DA-BILL), but does not audit or fix the billing import validation rules. Release was held because DA-RULES completeness is unknown while the release assumes completeness, and Layer 1 verification failed (scope does not address root problem and limitations are not honestly stated). The release omits auditing or fixing the billing import validation rules, which are identified as the root cause, and does not explicitly state this limitation, assuming validation alone is sufficient.
